equivalence_model.story_stripped_kernel: For exchangeable cyclic spacings, count gaps that are smaller than both adjacent gaps. Each such local-minimum gap corresponds exactly to a mutual nearest-neighbour pair; by symmetry each gap is locally minimal with probability 1/3.

mutual nearest neighbours ↔ reflexive nearest-neighbour pairs
mutual pair ↔ local minimum of three consecutive spacings
circle version ↔ Stage-3 merged line-segment variant

findings.source: Selim Bahadır and Elvan Ceyhan, On the Number of Reflexive and Shared Nearest Neighbor Pairs in One-Dimensional Uniform Data
findings.relationship: For uniform one-dimensional data, proves E(R_n)=n/3 and represents reflexive pairs via local-minimum spacings; cites earlier 1999 work for the same expectation.
findings.notes: This is the Stage-3 merged line formulation and uses the same statistic and local-spacing mechanism.

findings.source: Theoretical Computer Science Stack Exchange — Number of connected components of a random nearest neighbor graph?
findings.relationship: Uses a wrap-around metric (the circle), identifies a mutual pair exactly when the middle of three consecutive gaps is smallest, and obtains probability 1/3 / expectation n/3.
findings.notes: This is essentially the frozen circle kernel, including the same proof idea.

gaps: The full historical nearest-neighbour literature was not exhaustively reconstructed once exact equivalent results were located.

classification_rationale: The n/3 expectation for mutual/reflexive nearest-neighbour pairs in one-dimensional uniform data is established, and a public wrap-around formulation reproduces the circle/local-minimum argument. The mathematical content is already known.
